guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Paediatric Basic Life Support 2021
title: Child pulled from a stream at a country fayre
setting: Country fayre by a stream. A 6-year-old girl was found floating face down and pulled out by her father moments ago. Unresponsive and not breathing.
verdictExplanation: An unresponsive, non-breathing child after immersion. Paediatric cardiac arrest secondary to drowning. Critically sick: this needs immediate paediatric resuscitation starting with rescue breaths.

shared.airway: Can be opened, child cannot maintain own airway

history.history: Found floating face down, seen on dry land minutes earlier
history.additional: Pulled from the water by her father

followUp.question: How does your resuscitation start for this child?

options.text: Give 5 initial rescue breaths, then 15 compressions to 2 breaths; send for help and the AED
Start with 30 compressions before any breaths, as for an adult
Roll her straight into the recovery position to drain water
Hold her upside down and slap her back to clear the lungs

followUp.explanation: Paediatric arrest from drowning is hypoxic, so begin with 5 rescue breaths, then continue 15:2. Draining water and inverting the child waste time and risk harm. Get help and the AED on the way without delaying CPR.

levelExplanation.cfa: If you are alone, give 1 minute of CPR before leaving to call for help.
levelExplanation.er: Manage the airway with your adjuncts, give oxygen if available and keep her warm to limit further cooling.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Paediatric sequence differs from adults: airway and breathing first because the cause is usually hypoxic.
